reason: E2 directly supports that Mn addition causes magnetic frustration which breaks the trend for relative hcp vs fcc energies, and that CrCoNi has an hcp ground state, supporting premises 1, 2, and 5. However, the cited evidence does not address the deformation-induced, dislocation-triggered nature of the transformation (premise 3) or the role of nanoscale hcp as obstacles enhancing strain hardening (premise 4); E1 and E3 are irrelevant to these mechanistic claims.
premises: Removing Mn reduces magnetic frustration in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloys
Reduced magnetic frustration lowers the barrier for fcc-to-hcp transformation at stacking faults and twin boundaries
The fcc-to-hcp transformation is dislocation-triggered and occurs during deformation
Nanoscale hcp regions act as obstacles to dislocation motion, enhancing strain hardening
The CrCoNi ternary alloy exhibits an hcp ground state, unlike the quinary alloy
